Dear Appeals Coordinator:

I am writing to formally appeal HMSA's denial of prior authorization for lumbar fusion (CPT 22612), as stated in the notice referenced above. HMSA's stated reason for denial is: "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree and ask that HMSA reverse this determination, because the imaging and clinical record submitted with my request directly satisfy the medical-necessity criteria that HMSA's own vendor, Evolent (which HMSA's provider materials confirm "authorizes on behalf of HMSA" for musculoskeletal/spine surgery precertification via RadMD), applies to lumbar fusion requests.

**Sourcing note on the policy quoted below:** The specific medical-necessity criteria quoted in this appeal are taken verbatim from Evolent's "Lumbar Spine Surgery" clinical guideline (the guideline covering CPT 22612 under "Lumbar Fusion – Single Level," guideline number Evolent_CG_1766, successor to the prior guideline number NIA_CG_304), as I was able to retrieve it. I was not able to load, in full, the identical HMSA-letterhead copy of this guideline through HMSA's own RadMD‑hosted PDF before it was cut off during retrieval; the language quoted below comes from a copy of the same Evolent national guideline (same title, same CPT-code list, same guideline lineage) published through a separate public regulatory filing. If HMSA applied a different or more current version of this guideline to my request, I ask that HMSA identify that version and provide me a full copy, as I am entitled to under my appeal rights, and I reserve the right to supplement this appeal once I receive it. Any text below that is not in quotation marks is my own summary or argument, not the plan's language.

**1. The criteria for single-level lumbar fusion, and how my record meets them**

The guideline states that single-level lumbar fusion is indicated:

"When ALL of the following are present: Lumbar back pain, neurogenic claudication, and/or radicular leg pain without sensory or motor deficit that impairs daily activities for at least 6 months ... Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months ... Imaging studies corresponding to the clinical findings ... At least ONE of the following clinical conditions: Spondylolisthesis (neural arch defect - spondylolytic spondylolisthesis, degenerative spondylolisthesis, and congenital unilateral neural arch hypoplasia) ... Evidence of segmental instability - Excessive motion, as in degenerative spondylolisthesis, segmental instability, and surgically induced segmental [instability]."

My submitted record satisfies each element:

- *Duration and functional impairment:* I have had 18 months of progressive low back and leg pain, unrelieved by rest, which exceeds the guideline's 6‑month duration requirement. I cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop, relieved only by sitting — this is documented neurogenic claudication that impairs daily activities.

- *Failure of conservative treatment:* I completed 18 visits of supervised physical therapy (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility) over 12 weeks, from 2026-03-23 to 2026-06-15, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note — well beyond the guideline's minimum of six consecutive weeks in the last six months. I also used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-20 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned. This is a documented failure of multiple conservative modalities to produce lasting improvement.

- *Imaging corresponding to clinical findings:* MRI of the lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiographs on 2026-06-15 show grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina. On examination, I have neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes — findings that directly correspond to the L4-L5 level identified on imaging.

- *At least one qualifying clinical condition:* My imaging shows two of the specific conditions the guideline lists as qualifying findings — (a) "Spondylolisthesis (neural arch defect - spondylolytic spondylolisthesis, degenerative spondylolisthesis...)," documented as grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5; and (b) "Evidence of segmental instability - Excessive motion, as in degenerative spondylolisthesis, segmental instability," documented as 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension radiographs. Either finding independently satisfies this element of the guideline.

Given that my imaging affirmatively demonstrates both degenerative spondylolisthesis and radiographic segmental instability at the symptomatic level, together with 18 months of correlating clinical symptoms and documented failure of physical therapy, NSAIDs, and injection therapy, the stated basis for denial — that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure" — is not consistent with the record submitted or with the plan's own guideline for this exact clinical scenario.

**2. Absence of disqualifying factors**

I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke — none of which are described in the material I have as barriers to surgical candidacy.

**3. Requested action**

I ask that HMSA:
1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 22612 (lumbar fusion) as requested by Dr. Okafor;
2. If HMSA relied on a different, more current, or differently worded version of its lumbar spine surgery guideline in reaching this determination, provide me a complete copy of the specific guideline document and version applied to my request, including its title, guideline/policy number, and effective date, as part of the claim file I am entitled to review; and
3. If HMSA still intends to uphold the denial, provide a written, criterion-by-criterion explanation of which specific requirement(s) in that guideline my submitted imaging and clinical records are said not to meet.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of: the physical therapy discharge note (12 weeks, 18 visits, 2026-03-23 to 2026-06-15); documentation of NSAID use (8 months) and the corticosteroid injection of 2026-03-20; the MRI and flexion-extension radiograph reports dated 2026-06-15; and Dr. Okafor's clinical notes documenting neurogenic claudication, functional limitation, and bilateral L5 sensory changes.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the timeframe for HMSA's decision. If the delay associated with standard appeal review threatens to seriously harm my health or functioning, I may separately request an expedited appeal.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,
